neighbours.label: the token right after a lone punctuation mark that stands by itself as a name or string ('/', '_', '-', '.'): fires on what follows the bare symbol, not when the symbol starts a longer path or identifier
fire: To mount the disk at boot, set its mount point to / in the installer and reboot.

from django.utils.translation import gettext
_ = gettext
title = _("Welcome")
The date parts are glued together with '-', so you get 2020-01-31.
By default the fields are separated by '_', which you can change in the settings.
After chroot the process sees the new directory as / (and cannot climb out of it).
quiet: To mount the disk at boot, set its mount point to /mnt/data in the installer and reboot.

from django.utils.translation import gettext
translate = gettext
title = translate("Welcome")
The date parts are glued together with dashes, so you get 2020-01-31.
version = sep.join(str(n) for n in numbers)
By default the fields are separated by underscores, which you can change in the settings.
After chroot the process sees the new directory as its root (and cannot climb out of it).

notes: Card: top examples follow a bare '/', '_', '-', '.' or '--' in code strings and prose. Probes: bare '/' 0.66-0.69, '_ =' 0.44, "'-'," 0.34, "'.'.join" 0.55; '/home/user' 0.01, '"/index"' 0.09, 'tr =' 0.01. Near misses keep the same code or prose but the symbol is part of a longer path or name.
